title: Pointers, arrays and address arithmetic
goal: Traverse an array range through pointers after validating the logical length used to compute its end.

prerequisites.text: You need logical array length, pointer dereferencing and the condition in a for loop.

terms.title: Range beginning
terms.definition: A pointer to the first cell of the prepared array. For an empty range it equals the end.

terms.title: Exclusive end
terms.definition: The boundary just after the range’s last element. It can be within the array capacity or one position beyond the full array.

terms.title: Offset
terms.definition: The number of elements from the start of the array. Adding an integer to a pointer advances it by that many elements of the pointed-to type.

sections.title: The boundary where traversal stops
paragraphs: To walk through readings, keep a pointer cursor to the current item and end at the position after the used items. Check cursor != end before reading through *cursor.
In begin = readings the array name converts to a pointer to its first element. Adding 1 advances one element because the pointer type determines the stride.

When the working length equals capacity, end points one past the full array. Use this position as a boundary when comparing pointers within the same array. End the loop before reading through end. When length is zero, begin already equals end on the first check.

sections.title: Sum three readings and an empty range
paragraphs: Picture offsets 0, 1, 2 and 3. Only the first three positions hold values. At position 3 the loop stops before reading.
steps: The assignments in main give begin offset 0 and end offset 3.
Each iteration checks cursor != end first. It then adds the value to total and advances the pointer by one element.
The second call passes begin twice. The body is skipped and the result is 0.

sections.title: Offsets and the valid range
paragraphs: Clang rejects cursor += 0.5. A pointer offset must be an integer number of elements.

The exercise validates length from 0 through capacity before computing end. The expression end - 1 points at the last used element only for a nonempty range. If the range is empty and begin is the array start, even computing begin - 1 is outside the allowed range.

sections.title: Vary the length while keeping capacity
paragraphs: Imagine a four-cell buffer holding 4, 8, 7 and 9. Write the end offset and the number of matching readings with working lengths 0, 2 and 4. Use an inclusive threshold of 8.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check array conversion, permitted offsets and pointer comparison rules.

selfcheck.prompt: After summing three elements, cursor equals end. What happens next?
options: The condition ends the loop before any read
Move the pointer one more element
feedback: The condition checks for the end before the body can run.
A false condition skips any further advance.

selfcheck.prompt: The working length is 0 and begin points at the first array element. Can you compute end - 1?
options: Yes, if you do not read through it
No, it would be before the array
feedback: Even computing the result goes outside the allowed range.
Casting does not create a valid array position.
end equals begin, so a step backward is outside the array.

selfcheck.prompt: The buffer holds 4, 8, 7 and 9 with working length 2. Which elements do you read with threshold 8, and what count do you get?
selfcheck.feedback: You read only 4 and 8 and count 8. end has offset 2, so 7 and 9 are never read.

practice.title: Count readings through pointers
practice.task: The first line gives a reading count from 0 to 4. Read exactly that many integers from -99 to 99, one per line. Ignore later lines. Print the number of readings at least 8. Print invalid for a missing record, malformed number or length outside 0 through 4. In count_at_least, walk from the array beginning to its validated exclusive end.
practice.hint: Find which position end denotes after begin + length. Compare it with the boundary used by the starter.
criteria: The four values 1, 7, 8 and 9 give 2. A zero length gives 0.
A match at the last position is counted.
Capacity is validated before computing end, and the loop compares to end before dereferencing.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: Save a copy of your corrected main.c in a separate text file. In the editor, change the threshold to 4. Try length 3 followed by 3, 4 and 5 on separate lines. Restore your saved version afterward.
criteria: Output 2 shows that 4 and 5 both count.
The loop compares with end before accessing an element.
